ailurophilia n

Word of the day
for October 30
bothy n (chiefly Northern Ireland, Northumberland, Scotland)
  1. A small cottage or hut; specifically (Scotland), one often left unlocked for communal use in a remote, often mountainous, area by hikers, labourers, etc.
  2. A building for workers to rest in.
  3. (agriculture, historical) A building on a farm, sometimes with just one room, for (usually unmarried male) farmworkers or other labourers to live in.

The Gaelic festival of Samhain, which marks the end of the harvest season and the beginning of winter, begins on the night of 31 October and extends to 1 November.

Word of the day
for November 1
metonymy n
  1. (rhetoric)
    1. (uncountable) The use of a single characteristic or part of a concept, object, or phenomenon to identify the whole, or a related thing; also (semantics) the process of semantic association involved in interpreting or producing this.
    2. (countable) Synonym of metonym (“a term which identifies a concept, object, or phenomenon from a single characteristic or part of it, or from a related thing”).
  2. (by extension, countable) A thing which is used to represent or symbolize something else; a representation, a symbol.

The American singer Shirley Ellis released her song “The Name Game” this month in 1964.

entry.title: Word of the day for November 4
entry.summary:
edit · refresh · view
Word of the day
for November 4
lame duck n
  1. (idiomatic, informal, also attributive) A person or thing that is unable to function without assistance, or which is otherwise helpless, ineffective, or inefficient.
    1. (finance) A business which is not profitable or successful; specifically (originally and chiefly UK), a private business, industry, etc., which is unable to continue without financial assistance, especially from the government.
    2. (nautical) A ship which is unable to sail properly, especially because its means of propulsion is not working; (by extension) some other type of vehicle which is unable to run.
    3. (stock market, slang, dated) A person who invests or speculates in a stock market but is unable to fulfil their contracts.
    4. (originally US, politics) A politician regarded as ineffective or unsuccessful, especially one who lost an election; specifically, an elected official or politician, an administration, etc., that has lost an election or is not eligible for reelection, and is regarded as lacking political influence or power during the remainder of a term of office.
      1. (by extension) A person who is leaving a job, position, etc., soon, and so is regarded as lacking enthusiasm, influence, or power.
  2. (computing) A server that continues to serve ongoing requests while refusing new ones, allowing for a smooth shutdown.

lame duck v (informal)

  1. (transitive)
    1. Followed by the dummy pronoun it: to behave in the manner of a lame duck (noun senses).
      1. Especially of a machine, vehicle, etc.: to operate poorly or slowly; to falter.
      2. (often politics) To continue in a job, office, etc., during the remainder of a term there, while lacking enthusiasm, influence, or power.
    2. (dated) To help or look after (someone) who is or appears to be unable to function without assistance; also, to treat (someone) as helpless, ineffective, or inefficient; to mollycoddle, to pamper.
  2. (intransitive) To behave in the manner of a lame duck (noun senses).

Today is the day after Election Day for the 2026 United States elections.

Word of the day
for November 5
voir dire n (law)
  1. (Commonwealth, US) A separate hearing held in the course of a trial to determine some specific issue relevant to that trial, such as the admissibility of a piece of evidence or the competence of a witness to testify.
  2. (Commonwealth, US, criminal law, specifically) A preliminary hearing held without a jury to determine whether the evidence of a criminal offence is admissible such that the matter should go to trial.
  3. (US) The preliminary phase of a jury trial in which the jurors are examined and selected; impanelment.

Tomorrow, the first Friday of November in 2026, is Love Your Lawyer Day, which was established 25 years ago in 2001 by the American Lawyers Public Image Association.

Word of the day
for November 6
sax n (music, informal)
  1. Clipping of saxophone.
  2. Clipping of saxophonist.

sax v (music, informal)

  1. (transitive) Followed by the dummy pronoun it: to play the saxophone.
  2. (intransitive) To play the saxophone.

sax n

  1. (weaponry, obsolete except historical) A short sword used by Germanic peoples, especially the Saxons, from about the 4th to 10th centuries; a type of dagger; a seax; also, a type of knife or machete used as a cutting tool by these peoples.
  2. (by extension) A tool, similar to a hatchet, with an edge for cutting slate tiles for roofing, and a sharp point for making holes in the tiles for nails; a zax. [...]

The Belgian musician Adolphe Sax, who invented the saxophone, was born on this day in 1814.
